AnalysisDeclaration__identifier_optional.description: An analysis that this analysis uses, found by exactly one of `path` and `url`. Its elements are addressed through the declaration's id, as `<declaration>.<element>`.

commit.description: The full id of the commit the declared analysis is read at. A declaration with a `url` has one; with a `path`, it declares the analysis at that path as it was at that commit.

path.description: The directory of the declared analysis's `astra.yaml`, relative to the folder of this `astra.yaml` and inside the repository this file is read from, which in the working tree is the root's, submodules included. It is non-empty, doesn't start with `/` or `~`, separates folders with `/` (never `\`), and has no ASCII control character (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F); `..` segments are allowed.

url.description: Where git fetches another repository from, as a remote with no ASCII space or control character: `scheme://…`, such as `https://github.com/owner/analysis` or `file:///srv/repo`, or `[user@]host:path`, such as `git@github.com:owner/repo`. The declared analysis is the one at the top level of that repository, at `commit`.

AnalysisDeclaration__identifier_optional.title: AnalysisDeclaration

Decision__identifier_optional.description: A choice the analysis makes between options, such as which estimator to use.

label.description: A short display name for the decision.

options.description: The options the decision chooses between, keyed by id. There is at least one.

rationale.description: Why the analysis makes this decision, in free prose.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the decision.

when.description: The conditions under which the decision is active. It is active only when every condition holds.

Decision__identifier_optional.title: Decision

Evidence.description: What a claim rests on: a published work, cited by its `doi`, or an output, cited as an `artifact`. It has exactly one of the two, and a `version` only with a `doi`.

artifact.description: A reference to the cited output, written as in an output's `inputs`. It may pin the output to a universe, and should when the output is built per universe: to the universe the claim is about, such as `f1_score#svm_standard`.

doi.description: The DOI name of the cited work, under the `10` directory: `10.`, the registrant code, `/` and the suffix, such as `10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762`.

location.description: The place in the cited work or output the claim rests on, such as `page=6`.

quote.description: The passage of the cited work or output the claim rests on. With a `location`, the passage is sought within that place.

version.description: The version of the cited work, counted from 1, such as `2` for the second version of an arXiv paper.

Evidence.title: Evidence

FragmentSelector.description: A place in the cited work or output, given as a fragment identifier in the syntax `conforms_to` names, such as `row=5-7` in a CSV (RFC 7111). Without `conforms_to`, it is a PDF fragment identifier (RFC 8118 §3), such as `page=6`, with pages counted from 1.

conforms_to.description: The IRI of the specification of the fragment syntax `value` follows, as W3C Web Annotation gives it, such as `http://tools.ietf.org/rfc/rfc7111` for a CSV. Without it, `value` is a PDF fragment identifier (RFC 8118).

value.description: The fragment identifier, without the leading `#`, such as `page=6`. It is non-empty and holds no ASCII space or control character, none of ``"#<>[\]^`{|}``, and `%` only before two hex digits.

FragmentSelector.title: FragmentSelector

Input__identifier_optional.description: A file the analysis reads, tracked in git with it and named by its path.

description.description: What the input's data is, in free prose.

label.description: A short display name for the input.

path.description: The path of the input's file, relative to the folder of the `astra.yaml`. It is non-empty, doesn't start with `/` or `~`, separates folders with `/` (never `\`), has no `..` segment or ASCII control character (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F), and doesn't end in `/`.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the input.

Input__identifier_optional.title: Input

Insight__identifier_optional.description: A claim backed by evidence: as a prior insight, what earlier work establishes and the analysis builds on; as a finding, what the analysis concludes.

claim.description: What the insight asserts, in one or two sentences.

description.description: The reasoning behind the claim, in free prose.

evidence.description: What the claim rests on, as a list. There is at least one.

label.description: A short display name for the insight.

scope.description: The conditions under which the claim holds, in free prose.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the insight.

Insight__identifier_optional.title: Insight

Option__identifier_optional.description: One of the options a decision chooses between.

description.description: What the option is, in free prose.

excluded.description: Why the option is ruled out, as a reason that is not blank; any string is a reason, `no` and `off` included. An option with a reason is excluded: no universe selects it.

incompatible_with.description: The options that are never selected together with this option.

insights.description: The ids of the prior insights that support the option.

label.description: A short display name for the option.

requires.description: The options that are also selected whenever this option is.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the option.

Option__identifier_optional.title: Option

OutputType.description: The kind of artefact an output is.
OutputType.title: OutputType

Output__identifier_optional.description: An artefact the analysis makes, such as a metric, a figure or a table: what it is, what it is made from, and how.

decisions.description: The addresses of the decisions whose option the output is made with directly, not through what it reads: a different option for any of them, in the universe being built, can give a different result.

description.description: What the output is, in free prose.

format.description: How the output's artefact is encoded, as a lowercase token: the extension of its results' files, without the leading dot, such as `png`, `csv` or `parquet`. Any token that matches the pattern is a format.

inputs.description: What the output is made from, in order: references to inputs and outputs of the analysis or of analyses it declares. A reference to an output can be pinned to a universe with `#`; a reference to an input can't.

label.description: A short display name for the output.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the output.

type.description: The kind of artefact the output is.

when.description: The conditions under which the output is active. It is active only when every condition holds.

Output__identifier_optional.title: Output

Recipe.description:
A build rule that produces an output. A recipe is pure *how*: a `command` to invoke and the execution context (`resources`, `container`).
Recipes do not declare what the output depends on. Provenance — upstream inputs, decision-driven parameterization, and activation conditions — is declared on the parent Output (`inputs`, `decisions`, `when`). Runners surface the resolved input map and active decision values to the recipe via `{...}` template substitution (see `command`).

command.description:
The POSIX shell command that makes the output, such as `python src/train.py`. It is a template, whose placeholders a runner substitutes before running it:

  {inputs.<entry>}     the path of what an entry of the output's
                       `inputs` names, with <entry> written
                       exactly as the entry is, dots and `#`
                       included, as in
                       {inputs.classification.accuracy#baseline}
  {decisions.<entry>}  the id of the option selected for the
                       decision an entry of the output's
                       `decisions` names, with <entry> written
                       exactly as the entry is, as in
                       {decisions.iris.random_seed}
  {inputs}             the paths of all the output's inputs, in
                       the order of `inputs`, separated by spaces
  {output}             the path the result is written to
  {{ and }}            a literal { and }

Every placeholder takes one of these forms, and the <entry> of an {inputs.<entry>} or {decisions.<entry>} is an entry of the output's `inputs` or `decisions`, exactly as written.

container.description: Container image name or path to a Containerfile. Image names (e.g., 'python:3.9', 'ghcr.io/org/img:latest') are pulled as pre-built images; file paths (e.g., 'Containerfile', 'containers/Dockerfile') are built from source.

Recipe.title: Recipe

Resources.description: Compute resource requirements for a recipe. Values follow cloud-native conventions (string-with-units for sized quantities) so cluster executors can consume them directly.

cpus.description: CPU cores requested. Fractional values are allowed (e.g., 0.5) for runners that support CPU shares.

disk.description: Disk requirement as a string with units (e.g., '10Gi', '500Mi').

memory.description: Memory requirement as a string with units (e.g., '16Gi', '512Mi', '8GB').

time_limit.description: Maximum wall time as a duration string (e.g., '2h', '30m', '1h30m').

Resources.title: Resources

TextQuoteSelector.description: A passage of the cited work or output, quoted exactly, with the text just before and after it to tell it apart where the same words occur more than once.

exact.description: The passage, exactly as the cited work or output writes it.

prefix.description: The text that comes just before the passage.

suffix.description: The text that comes just after the passage.

TextQuoteSelector.title: TextQuoteSelector

Universe__identifier_optional.description: A universe: a selection of one option for every active decision of the analysis and of every analysis reached through a declaration that a universe of the analysis drives. Its effective selection is the effective selection of the universe it is derived from, if any, with its own `decisions` written over it decision by decision and every inherited selection of a decision that isn't active in the result dropped, so a universe that switches a decision on must set it.

additionalProperties.description: The id of the option selected for the decision.

decisions.description: The options the universe selects, as `<decision>: <option>`, one key per decision. Each key is the id of a decision of the analysis or, for a decision of another analysis, a flat key: the decision's address through the declarations, `<declaration>.<decision>`, such as `stage.method`, or another spelling of either.

derived_from.description: The id of another universe of the analysis, whose effective selection this universe's effective selection is built on, so that this universe gives only the decisions it changes.

description.description: What the universe is, in free prose.

label.description: A short display name for the universe. It is not inherited through `derived_from`.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the universe. They are not inherited through `derived_from`.

Universe__identifier_optional.title: Universe

description: An analysis: the files it reads, the artefacts it makes and the decisions it makes along the way. It is the content of an `astra.yaml` file.

analyses.description: The analyses this analysis uses, keyed by the id it addresses them by.

container.description: The default container for this analysis's recipes. Image names are pulled; file paths are built from source.

decisions.description: The choices the analysis makes, keyed by id.

description.description: What the analysis does, in free prose.

findings.description: What the analysis concludes, as insights keyed by id.

inputs.description: The files the analysis reads, keyed by id.

label.description: A short display name for the analysis.

outputs.description: The artefacts the analysis makes, keyed by id. There is at least one.

prior_insights.description: What earlier work establishes and the analysis builds on, as insights keyed by id. Options cite them in their `insights`.

spec_version.description: The version of the ASTRA specification the document is written against, such as `0.1.0`.

tags.description: Keywords for grouping and finding the analysis.

universes.description: The universes of the analysis, keyed by id.
